L'Oréal Paris Is Offering A$32,000 Grants to Women Leading Change in Tech — Here's How to Enter
sum: Women make up just 20 per cent of Australia’s highly technical workforce. After the age of 40, that falls to 16 per cent, according to the Tech Council of Australia, because women leave these roles at twice the rate of men. Across the wider economy, women still earn 21.1 per cent less than men, a gap worth A$28,356 a year, according to the Workplace Gender Equality Agency.
The women working to close those gaps rarely get the spotlight, or the funding. L’Oréal Paris wants to change that.

Entries for its first Women for Worth Award in Australia and New Zealand open on 10 November and close on 31 December 2026. Four leaders of not-for-profit programs that empower women will each receive an A$32,000 charitable grant, mentoring through the L’Oréal Paris network, and a national and global platform to share their story.
- Women & Tech (including AI): organisations supporting women in digital and technology fields
- Women & Sport: programs that lift participation, coaching pathways and leadership for women and girls
- Women & Culture (including cinema): organisations advancing women’s representation, voice and leadership in culture, the creative industries, media and education
- Men for Worth: men leading organisations committed to gender equality in those three fields, including school programs that engage boys and young men as allies

items.t: Asics Shares Down on Q3 Report
sum: Asics Corp. shares tumbled Friday after the company posted third quarter results that missed analysts' expectations.
The share price decline was the most since August 2024. At Friday's close, shares dropped 14.34 percent, or 700 points, to 4,180 yen.
- Asics Opens Innovation Lab at the University of Michigan's Ann Arbor Campus
- Nike's New CFO Brings 'Healthy Realism' to Financial Projections, Analysts Say

Asics saw strong demand across Europe, North America and Greater China. But while the company maintained its full-year operating income guidance at 195 billion yen, that fell short of analysts' consensus estimate of 199.72 billion.
Net sales for the third quarter were 805.1 billion yen, up from 625 billion yen a year ago. Profit for the quarter was 114.7 billion yen, up from 86.3 billion a year ago.

In performance running, the company said all regions showed sales growth, which was up 15.8 percent year-over-year. For SportStyle, sales rose 70 percent year-over-year, with North America, Europe and Oceania showing "significant sales growth," Asics said. And for Onitsuka Tiger, sales rose 34.6 percent year-over-year. Sales in Japan was driven by strong demand from inbound tourism, while Europe also showed significant sales growth.

Burberry Courts Younger Shoppers in China and US as First-Half Operating Profit Beats Forecasts
sum: British luxury brand Burberry Group reported adjusted operating profit of £62 million (about ¥12 billion) for the first half of fiscal 2027 (April-September), beating analysts' forecast of £44 million. Comparable store sales rose 4% year-on-year in the July-September quarter, exceeding the 3% average market estimate. A strategy of offering a broad range of affordable price points succeeded in attracting younger consumers in China and the US, bucking the broader luxury market slowdown.

Burberry shares rose as much as 9.9% in London Stock Exchange trading on the 12th, marking their biggest intraday gain since April. The stock closed up 8%. It was the fifth consecutive quarter of positive growth, signaling to investors that the turnaround plan is gaining traction.

By region, comparable store sales rose 5% in Greater China and 11% in the Americas. Europe and the Middle East, meanwhile, fell 1%, hit by a drop in tourist spending. First-half wholesale revenue rose 17% excluding currency effects, exceeding the company's own forecast. For the full year, Burberry expects growth of 10-12%.
Note: Regional sales are on a July-September comparable store basis. Wholesale revenue is for the first half.

CEO Joshua Schulman said in a call with reporters that "our strategy of offering enduring value and great products at a fair price is resonating strongly with Chinese customers." He explained that offering a wide range of price points within each category, including entry-level items, helped bring in new customers. He said affordable products captured demand as consumers grow weary of competitors' "extortionate pricing."

Burberry is pursuing a strategy of building a price "pyramid," from relatively affordable items such as scarves starting at £195 (about ¥41,000) and cotton-cashmere socks at £85 (about ¥18,000) to leather bags and coats priced above £9,000 (about ¥1.9 million). Lightweight jackets, gabardine trench coats and the brand's signature check-patterned "Knight" leather bag series drove sales.
On a call with investors and analysts, Schulman said that unlike two years ago, accessories including handbags and shoes are now attracting new customers. "We will never be a leather-led brand.

L'Oreal stock: Innovist deal adds detail to broad Q3 growth
sum: L'Oréal's third-quarter update added strategic depth to a broad growth profile after the group said it had closed the acquisition of a majority stake in Innovist, an Indian digital-first personal care company. The information appears in L'Oréal's October 22 sales release.

L'Oréal generated EUR 35.33 billion in sales in the first nine months through September 30, up 7.7 percent on a reported basis and 6.9 percent like for like. Third-quarter sales rose to EUR 11.56 billion, with adjusted like-for-like growth accelerating to 7.7 percent.

All four divisions and all five regions expanded in the nine-month period. Professional Products led the divisions with adjusted like-for-like growth of 12.3 percent, followed by Dermatological Beauty at 11.6 percent. L'Oréal Luxe grew 5.8 percent, while Consumer Products advanced 4.2 percent.

SAPMENA-SSA was the fastest-growing region at 15.8 percent on an adjusted like-for-like basis. Europe grew 7.0 percent and North America 6.3 percent, while Latin America posted 2.4 percent growth despite weakness in Mexico. Fragrances and haircare remained key drivers, with skincare also accelerating.

Alongside the Innovist transaction, L'Oréal said its BOLD venture fund and Nykaa had agreed to take minority stakes in high-growth Indian beauty, personal care and wellness brands. The group also signed a memorandum of understanding with Cosmax on next-generation beauty innovation.

L'Oréal stock traded at 445.70 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:13 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026, 0.28 percent below the Xetra close of 446.95 euros on Wednesday, November 11. The quote was below the previous report's 447.00 euros at 12:29 CET, a separate comparison from the Xetra session move.

Why is e.l.f. Beauty (ELF) stock soaring today
sum: Shares of cosmetics company e.l.f. Beauty (NYSE:ELF) jumped 8.5% in the afternoon session after the company reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 results that came in above Wall Street estimates and raised its full-year outlook.

According to the company's release, revenue was $520.8 million, up 51.4% year on year, above S&P analysts' estimates of $475.3 million. Adjusted earnings were $1.21 a share, above estimates of 60 cents. Adjusted EBITDA was $123.4 million, above estimates of $76.8 million. The company raised its full-year revenue outlook to about $2.02 billion at the midpoint, above estimates, from $1.95 billion. It raised its full-year adjusted earnings outlook to about $3.84 at the midpoint, and its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to about $424 million, above estimates of $408.6 million.
Is now the time to buy e.l.f. Beauty? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

e.l.f. Beauty's shares are extremely volatile and have had 31 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 5 months ago when the stock gained 6.4% on the news that markets rotated into defensive names following the release of the May CPI report.

The headline 4.2% annual inflation reading spooked the market, but the breakdown matters: energy drove more than 60% of May's monthly price increase, while food at home rose just 0.1% and core inflation came in at only 0.2% for the month. For staples companies whose input costs are food, packaging, and household goods that is a margin reprieve.The World Cup, which kicks off later in the week across U.S., Mexican, and Canadian host cities, added a near-term catalyst. Goldman Sachs has buy ratings on AB InBev, Constellation Brands, and Heineken specifically on tournament beer demand.

e.l.f. Beauty is up 51.6% since the beginning of the year, and at $118.00 per share, it has set a new 52-week high. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of e.l.f. Beauty's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $3,811.

Skills, access to capital key to women's role in economy
sum: At the 29th Sustainable Development Conference, experts called for women’s skills programmes to connect participants with employment, customers and financing, while accounting for unpaid care duties, The Express Tribune reported. MNA Shaista Pervaiz Malik said relevant training, safe access to public spaces, market connections and capital were important to raising women’s participation in economic activity.

L’Oreal Pakistan CEO Rehan Saeed said women account for about half of the population but their labour force participation is around 24%. He argued that training has greater value when paired with jobs, mentoring and support for businesses; speakers also urged stronger workplace harassment protections and action on the legal and social obstacles women face.

UNDP’s Van Nguyen described a Vietnam initiative that connected women entrepreneurs to digital tools, markets and mentoring through 100 cooperatives. Former Punjab Social Protection Authority vice chair Jahan Ara Manzoor Wattoo said the Khud Mukhtar programme gives young married couples productive assets worth up to Rs150,000, including livestock, tools or business equipment.
- Experts called for skills programmes to connect women with jobs, markets and finance.
- Khud Mukhtar provides productive assets worth up to Rs150,000 to young married couples.

items.t: L'Oreal stock: Fragrance drives luxury growth after strong Q3
sum: L'Oreal's third-quarter performance is drawing fresh attention to fragrance demand, which the beauty group identified as the primary growth engine for its luxury business. The detail adds to the evidence that premium beauty remains a key support for the company's expansion.

According to eMarketer, L'Oreal's like-for-like sales rose 7.2 percent in the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Growth extended across all business divisions, while fragrance demand was particularly important for luxury brands including Armani, Prada and Yves Saint Laurent.

The category mix matters for investors because luxury products can support both sales momentum and the group's positioning in premium beauty. At the same time, eMarketer noted that shoppers are becoming more selective and increasingly consider product ingredients and effectiveness, raising the pressure on brands to substantiate marketing claims.

L'Oreal's earlier third-quarter update showed reported sales of 11.56 billion euros and adjusted like-for-like growth of 7.7 percent after accounting for the timing of an internal information-technology transformation. The unadjusted like-for-like rate was 7.2 percent, making the distinction relevant when assessing the underlying comparison.

Emma Walmsley named new HP chief, set to take office as CEO next January... shares surge 6%
sum: HP has appointed former GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) CEO Emma Walmsley as its next chief executive officer. Walmsley will take office on January 4, 2027, and HP's stock price rose more than 6% following the announcement.

U.S. computer and printer manufacturer HP has ended its nine-month interim CEO system and appointed Emma Walmsley as its next chief executive officer. The HP board of directors announced on the 4th (local time) that it had unanimously selected Walmsley as the new CEO. Walmsley's official start date is January 4, 2027. Bruce Broussard, who is currently serving as interim CEO, will move to the position of board chair on the same day, succeeding current chair Chip Bergh. Following the news of the appointment, HP's stock price surged more than 6% that day.

Walmsley served as CEO of GSK Group, leading the company from April 2017 to December 2025. Before joining GSK, she worked at L'Oreal for about 17 years, and at GSK, she served as CEO of the Consumer Healthcare division before becoming group CEO. She also served on the board of directors at Microsoft for seven years. Based on her experience in managing global consumer goods and healthcare companies and serving on the boards of technology firms, she will lead HP's PC, printer, software, and services businesses.

L'Oreal stock: All four divisions grow in Q3 2026
sum: L'Oréal's third-quarter performance added fresh evidence that growth is broadening across its portfolio. According to Playbook of Beauty, the company reported third-quarter sales of 11.56 billion euros for the period ended September 30, 2026, up 11.9 percent on a reported basis.

Adjusted like-for-like sales growth reached 7.7 percent in the quarter, compared with 6.5 percent in the first half. All four divisions expanded: Professional Products and Dermatological Beauty each grew 13.9 percent, Luxe advanced 7.0 percent and Consumer Products increased 3.8 percent.

Professional Products benefited from premium haircare, salon services and omnichannel distribution. Dermatological Beauty continued to gain from La Roche-Posay, CeraVe and SkinCeuticals. In Luxe, fragrances led growth, while Consumer Products saw accelerating volume development.

The regional picture was also uneven but broadly positive. SAPMENA-SSA led with adjusted like-for-like growth of 19.5 percent, followed by Europe at 8.9 percent, North Asia at 7.8 percent and North America at 5.6 percent. Latin America declined 3.0 percent, affected by temporary makeup supply disruptions and distributor stock adjustments in Mexico.

Nine-month sales reached 35.34 billion euros, up 6.9 percent on both like-for-like and adjusted like-for-like measures, according to the same report. E-commerce grew around 17 percent over the first nine months, adding support to L'Oréal's omnichannel strategy.

Chief Executive Nicolas Hieronimus said the first nine months gave him confidence that L'Oréal would deliver another year of sales and profit growth. The company expects the global beauty market to grow by about 5 percent in the fourth quarter and aims to continue outperforming it, albeit at a more moderate pace than in the third quarter.

Kristen Bell Owns Her Worth as L’Oréal Paris’ Newest Global Ambassador
sum: L’Oréal Paris has announced that Emmy-nominated actress and producer Kristen Bell is its newest global ambassador.

Timed to the announcement, Bell appears in her debut campaign displaying a mix of her confidence and wit by introducing herself as the brand’s global ambassador on her own terms with L’Oréal Paris’ signature “You’re Worth It” tag line.

“‘You’re Worth It’ isn’t something L’Oréal Paris gave women — the worth was always ours,” said Bell. “What they gave us was permission to say it out loud. That’s the part that gets me. It isn’t about being made to feel valuable. It’s about a brand that handed women the mic before anyone else thought to.”

L’Oréal Paris said the actress’ authentic authority is what made her the “natural choice” to front the message for the campaign. The partnership between the two is an alignment in values — with beauty seen as both an active, daily choice and an expression of self-authorship. Moreover, L’Oréal Paris said the collaboration is “deeply rooted” in women’s everyday lives by leveraging high-caliber storytelling and accessibility with its range of products.

The debut campaign captures the essence of Bell by switching between chic, elevated vignettes and unpolished moments about her own daily life. Then, Bell takes over her own introduction to champion the idea that confidence lies in embracing the complex reality of ourselves.

“Kristen is a true force — she blends an unapologetic self-assurance with a genuine, down-to-earth warmth that immediately commands respect and connection,” said Laura Branik, president of L’Oréal Paris USA. “Welcoming her to L’Oréal Paris is a defining moment. This partnership isn’t just about showcasing incredible, trusted products; it’s about amplifying a powerful voice that inspires every woman to own her narrative and confidently define her own worth.”

Bell said that growing up she remembers “sneaking into [her] mom’s vanity, stealing five minutes with her L’Oréal Paris lipstick” before she was caught. Looking back, that moment was more so about trying on who Bell could be rather than the lipstick itself.

L’Oréal stock rallies as third-quarter sales beat estimates
sum: Investing.com -- L'Oréal shares rose more than 3% Friday after the French beauty group reported third-quarter sales that comfortably exceeded analyst expectations, with growth accelerating across all four divisions and most regions.

Sales rose 12% year over year to €11.56 billion in the three months to September, beating the €11.24 billion consensus estimate. Like-for-like sales growth reached 7.7%, well above the 5.43% expected by analysts, according to Bloomberg consensus data.

Professional Products and Dermatological Beauty led the outperformance, each delivering 13.9% like-for-like growth. Professional Products beat the 8.78% estimate, while Dermatological Beauty exceeded expectations for 10.3% growth. L'Oréal Luxe sales rose 7%, ahead of the 4.11% forecast, while Consumer Products grew 3.8%, marginally above the 3.74% estimate.

"L'Oréal delivered an exceptional third quarter as adjusted like-for-like growth accelerated to 7.7%," Chief Executive Nicolas Hieronimus said. "The global beauty market, once again, proved its resilience in a challenging context – and we continued to significantly outpace it."

Regional performance was broadly strong. SAPMENA-SSA, covering South Asia Pacific, the Middle East, North Africa and sub-Saharan Africa, led with like-for-like growth of 19.5%, well above the 11.8% consensus estimate. Europe grew 8.9%, compared with expectations of 5.41%, while North Asia advanced 7.8%, against a forecast of 4.14%. North American sales rose 5.6%, also beating estimates.
Latin America was the sole regional miss, with sales declining 3% against expectations for 6% growth. L'Oréal attributed the weakness to commercial issues and supply-chain disruptions in Mexico.
For the first nine months of 2026, sales totaled €35.33 billion, up 7.7% on a reported basis and 6.9% like-for-like. E-commerce sales grew approximately 17%, outpacing the online market.

USF team makes U.S. finals in global L’Oréal Brandstorm competition
sum: NEW YORK — Three University of South Florida students competed in the national finals of the 2026 L’Oréal Brandstorm competition, earning the opportunity to present their concept to executives at L’Oréal’s New York headquarters in mid-April.
The USF team was one of five finalist teams in the United States.

Representing USF as team “Mémoire Vive,” Jaycee Cavero of the Muma College of Business, Samin Yasar and Prithvi Kota from USF’s College of Arts and Sciences competed alongside students from institutions including New York University, the University of California, Berkeley, Parsons School of Design and Fashion Institute of Technology in the global innovation competition focused on shaping the future of luxury fragrance.
According to the team, their success was built long before the competition itself.

“Samin and I have known each other for a few years, and we met Jaycee about a year before Brandstorm,” said Kota. “The three of us ended up in the same USF Global Career Accelerator cohort, where we placed in the top 10 in early talent competitions, so when it came time to build a three-person team, he was an obvious fit.”
What followed was a collaboration built around trust, complementary skillsets and constant iteration.

“Jaycee led marketing and product design, I anchored conservation science and logistics, and Samin drove pricing and quantitative modeling,” Kota explained. “Every decision was still a shared one, but knowing each other beforehand meant we could be direct with feedback without worrying about hurting anyone’s feelings, which kept the iteration loop fast.”

items.t: L’Oréal USA’s CEO on Brand, Beauty and Leadership
sum: Alexis Perakis-Valat, chief executive officer of L’Oréal USA, has hit the ground running in parent company L’Oréal’s biggest market — and also hit the road.

“I’ve been on shop floors, on plant floors, I’ve talked to a lot of our employees, and I’ve had tons of meetings with our teams and with retail partners, which is absolutely fascinating,” Perakis-Valat said in conversation with Jenny B. Fine, WWD executive editor, beauty and editor in chief of Beauty Inc. “After 32 years at L’Oréal, I keep learning and discovering so many new things, and the first observation is that L’Oréal in the U.S. is both a concentration of what L’Oréal does at its best and at the same time, a demonstration of our ability to adapt to the specificities of a market.”

The beauty giant markets more than 35 brands in the U.S., and a touch less than half of the business is done with American brands. “The other half is done with French brands, Italian brands and, maybe one day, Korean brands. That’s what we like at L’Oréal — to be able to portray this diversity [in geographies], and also in prices. We were super happy to have Kering Beauté and Creed join our family and we’re equally happy to be able to offer home hair color for less than $5 under the Garnier brand.”

L’Oréal holds 14 percent market share in the U.S., and thinking of the company as an underdog is what pushes Perakis-Valat to keep driving gains. “We are thinking like challengers, we hate complacency, we don’t want to be arrogant, and we don’t want to give advice to amazingly creative people,” he said. “What is also interesting is that what we did in this country is adapt to the specificities of the U.S.”

Case in point, SalonCentric was born out of a U.S.-specific need to optimize the ever-fragmented professional hair care channel. “Now we have 800 stores across the country for stylists and it gives us this contact with the professionals that shape our industry,” Perakis-Valat said. “It gives us a lot of insight, and it’s a great example of how you can create new things that are not in the current playbook to adapt to a situation.”
As he’s thinking about the integrations of AI at L’Oréal USA, Perakis-Valat is also drawing upon past digital revolutions he’s been a part of.

Delhivery stock falls 3.5% as Amazon launches global supply chain services
sum: Delhivery shares were under pressure on Wednesday, falling as much as 3.5% in early trade a day after Amazon launched its supply chain services globally, raising competition concerns in India's logistics arena.

On Tuesday, Amazon said it would allow other businesses to store and ship goods ranging from raw materials to final products through its vast network. The ecommerce giant aims to challenge the US market, long dominated by UPS and FedEx.
Shares of FedEx and UPS fell more than 9% each during Monday trade, while Amazon rose nearly 1% on the NYSE.

Amazon Supply Chain Services opens the ecommerce giant's freight, distribution, fulfillment, and parcel shipping capabilities to businesses of all types and sizes, directly competing with third-party logistics providers.
The service is being positioned as the AWS of logistics, with early adopters including Procter & Gamble.
The company boasts a fleet of more than 100 cargo planes — behind only FedEx and UPS — along with a vast network of warehouses and sorting hubs.
For Delhivery, which competes for B2B and B2C logistics contracts, this means a threat from a well-capitalised rival with an established and wide network.

L’Oréal Group Revenues Rise 7.6% in Q1
sum: L’Oréal Group’s revenues rose 7.6% like-for-like to €12.2 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2026, beating analyst expectations. This was an acceleration from the last quarter, when L’Oréal missed expectations.

“We not only outperformed a beauty market that remains dynamic, but accelerated our market share gains around the world,” CEO Nicolas Hieronimus said in a statement. “Driven by the step-up in our innovation plan, we continue to win in fragrances, haircare, and makeup, and start seeing some encouraging signs in skincare. And our e-commerce leadership allows us to double down on the winning channel with spectacular results across all regions, especially emerging markets.”

On March 31, L’Oréal completed its acquisition of Kering Beauté, including House of Creed, as well as fifty-year exclusive licenses for the creation, development, and distribution of fragrances and beauty products under Bottega Veneta and Balenciaga.

By division, L’Oréal’s professional products (including Kerastase and Redken) sales saw the strongest uptick, rising 15.5% year-on-year, followed by dermatological beauty (including Cerave and La Roche-Posay), up 10.8%. Consumer products (including L’Oréal Paris and Maybelline) were up 5.8%, and luxe products (including Kiehl’s and Yves Saint Laurent) rose 5.2%.

By region, sales in Europe (up 10.3%), North America (up 11.4%), and emerging markets (South Asia Pacific, Middle East, North Africa, and Sub-Saharan Africa) drove growth, the latter up 20.4%. Latin America revenues rose 5.1%, while North Asia revenues fell 4%.

“The second half recovery in our two largest countries, the US and China, continued, and we outpaced the market in both,” Hieronimus said. “Despite current geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainties, we are optimistic about the outlook for the global beauty market. Our multi-polar model, the determination of our teams, as well as our innovation power, make me confident that we will continue to outperform and achieve another year of growth in sales and profit.”

Why L’Oréal Paris, Nyx and MAC are dominating TikTok beauty
sum: - Recent data has shown that beauty content posted by influencers on TikTok increases a brand’s earned media value.
- Makeup and skin care content rank higher, while fragrance shows increasing potential.
- UK and European rankings reveal that brands can rapidly rise or fall year-over-year depending on their social media strategy and audience response.

A recent report ranking the top 100 beauty brands on TikTok in the UK and Europe shows that success on the platform not only hinges on posting more content, but on how strongly audiences respond to it. Makeup and skin care content are ranking higher than fragrance, but outlier brands suggest the category has growth potential.

The Kolsquare report analyzes the performance of TikTok posts in Q4 of 2025, using data from the company’s own platform to track influencer posts mentioning beauty brands. In total, 247,173 TikTok posts were analyzed from October to December last year.

The influencer marketing company uses Earned Media Value (EMV) to determine the top 100 rankings. The metric assigns a monetary value to the audience engagement a brand receives from influencers’ TikTok posts, such as likes, comments, and shares. EMV helps estimate how much a post’s organic visibility would be worth if it were paid for.

According to the report, brands Nyx and L’Oréal Paris lead the top 100 rankings in the UK and Europe, respectively. The companies collaborate with large numbers of influencers and generate thousands of posts, which drives a high EMV for them.

The move reflects a broader reckoning in beauty, where discovery and purchase are increasingly happening on TikTok and Instagram, making social a key commerce channel.

sum: India, which currently contributes roughly one per cent of L'Oreal's turnover, is very small and needs a lot of effort, both financial and human, to change gears in India, Hieronimus said

French cosmetics major L'Oreal is "not satisfied" with its performance in the Indian market, where it has not gained any market share in 2025 despite recording high single-digit growth, said its global CEO Nicolas Hieronimus.
"India, though, is not meeting expectations, and we have a new setup there starting this year," said Hieronimus in his opening remarks.
Hieronimus said he is "optimistic, ambitious" that the company will start doing better in 2026.

L'Oreal, which last year appointed a new team, with Jacques Lebel as its India country manager, expects a growth revival in India, where beauty products are witnessing faster growth, riding on tailwinds as a growing economy, rising disposable income, and an expanding number of millennials.

When asked how L'Oreal is changing India going forward, he said the company has revised its strategy and is looking for major growth opportunities. The company expects to do better in the Indian market in 2026, he said.

"As far as India is concerned, when I say that, I am not satisfied. We had high single-digit growth, but we did not gain a lot of market share, if any. And in the end, I think it's just because we are setting up a new team, a new organisation," Hieronimus said.

items.t: L'Oreal shares slide as China sales disappoint
sum: L’Oréal shares slid in early Paris trading on Friday after the world’s biggest beauty group reported fourth-quarter sales that fell short of expectations, weighed down by a weaker-than-anticipated performance in North Asia and a slowdown in travel retail.

The company said like-for-like sales rose 6% in the quarter to about €11.25bn to €11.3bn, slightly below the consensus forecast of roughly 6.3% to 6.5%, prompting analysts to question whether top-line momentum can accelerate meaningfully in 2026.

For 2025, L’Oréal reported sales of €44.05bn, up 4% like-for-like and 1.3% on a reported basis, with management highlighting a broad-based second-half improvement led by a recovery in the US and China.
Currency moves were a notable drag, with the group citing a negative 3.6% impact on reported revenue.

CEO Nicolas Hieronimus said the company delivered “strong results regardless of the context” and argued that a stepped-up launch plan and a gradually improving beauty market supported a quarter-by-quarter acceleration through the year.
L’Oréal’s gross margin rose to 74.3% and operating margin increased to 20.2%, while earnings per share edged up 0.4% to €12.71.
The board proposed a dividend of €7.20 per share, up 2.9%, and said net cash flow rose 7.8% to about €7.2bn.

sum: L’Oréal Paris may be at the top of its game, but it’s entering 2026 in growth mode nonetheless.

The brand, which ranks number-one in beauty globally and is owned by the industry’s largest conglomerate — L’Oréal — was the top share gainer in U.S. mass hair care in 2025, according to NielsenIQ data provided by the brand, as well as a top-two makeup share gainer in the U.S. during the same period, according to Circana.

“Twenty twenty-five was one of our most successful years of the last five, if not 10 years,” said Laura Branik, president of L’Oréal Paris USA. “And that’s both in the consumer feedback we’ve gotten, as well as the sales data.”

She credits this acceleration to the brand’s twofold focus on innovative launches that “solve consumer pain points in a unique way,” as well as doubling down on longtime heroes like the Telescopic Mascara, which “continues to be strong and gain a new following.” The brand’s Infallible 3-second Setting Mist, Branik said, is also a global top-seller.

The brand is kicking off 2026 with no less than 20 launches across hair, skin care and makeup. Among them: an “age-defying” Serum Le Duo facial serum featuring two formulas in one bottle; a Revitalift eye bag eraser, which aims to instantly reduce the look of eye bags and can be applied directly to the skin or over makeup; new at-home hair dyes, and three hair care additions to its EverPure line.

In makeup, L’Oréal Paris is rolling out skin care-infused lip tints; blurring lip liners and lipsticks; an Extensionist mascara, and Lumi Bronze Soleil cream bronzer sticks, among other products. Prices range from $10.99 for the Colour Riche Blurred Matte Lipsticks to $15.99 for the Extensionist mascara.

Retail distribution across the newness varies: the Lip Contours will be exclusive to Ulta Beauty when they roll out Jan. 19, while Serum Le Duo is already available exclusively at Walmart. The Extensionist mascara, meanwhile, launched on TikTok Shop first before then rolling out to Ulta, Target and Amazon.

L'ORÉAL ADVANCES LEADERSHIP IN BEAUTY TECH BY BRINGING THE POWER OF INFRARED LIGHT TO HAIR AND SKIN WITH TWO BREAKTHROUGH INNOVATIONS AT CES® 2026
sum: Light Straight + Multi-styler and LED Face Mask, both CES® 2026 Innovation Award Honorees, harness unique light technology to augment hair and skin results

LAS VEGAS, Jan. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today at CES® 2026, L'Oréal Groupe, the world leader in beauty, introduced two breakthrough technologies that bring the power of light to haircare and skincare: Light Straight + Multi-styler and LED Face Mask, that have both been recognized as CES® 2026 Innovation Award honorees.

"At L'Oréal, we've always believed that beauty is deeply connected to scientific discovery, a belief that has been central to our company since its inception over 115 years ago. Today, we tirelessly combine the latest scientific and technological breakthroughs with our creativity to craft innovative beauty experiences that are more effective and tailored to individual needs. This year, our pioneering advancements in light technologies at CES 2026 once again demonstrate our commitment to pushing the boundaries of new beauty solutions," said Barbara Lavernos, Deputy CEO in charge of Research, Innovation and Technology at L'Oréal Groupe.

For over a century, hair straighteners have been an essential part of styling routines, but ordinary heating plates can reach temperatures of 400°F and higher—above the threshold at which keratin denatures, leading to weakened cuticles, breakage and reduced shine. This is a concern for consumers; according to a 2024 U.S. consumer study conducted by L'Oréal, 58% of women surveyed claimed their damaged hair had resulted from heat.

Developed by L'Oréal Research & Innovation, Light Straight + Multi-styler uses patented infrared light technology* to help provide exceptional styling results at lower temperatures, to better protect the health of the hair. Light Straight + Multi-styler's glass plates effectively straighten hair while never exceeding 320°F—a significant reduction compared to most traditional straighteners. According to instrumental tests conducted by L'Oréal, Light Straight + Multi-styler works 3X faster, and leaves hair 2X smoother, than leading premium hair stylers.
Light Straight + Multi-styler's streamlined user experience is the result of complex science and engineering.
